fix(chat): 14px reply action icons, duration after the actions

Code changes: +7 -5\
Tests: +6 -6\
Others: +0 -0

## What

- Reply action icons (copy, roll back) and the user-message edit/copy icons go from 12px to 14px.
- The turn duration moves from the start of a reply's action row to the end, after copy and roll back.

## Why

DESIGN.md sets default UI icons at 14–16px and keeps 12px for dense metadata. These are primary actions, so they should be 14px.

With the duration first, copy and roll back shifted right only on replies with no tool work (the ones where the time shows in the row instead of a "Worked for" fold). Putting it last keeps copy and roll back at the same spot on every reply.

#6884 put the time first. This keeps everything #6884 fixed (the time is still shown, and never twice) and only changes where it sits. @Annieeeee11, flagging in case you had a reason for leading with it.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Small 12px copy / roll back icons; on short replies the row reads "1m · copy · roll back". | 14px icons; the row reads "copy · roll back · 1m", so the icons stay in place across replies. |

Screenshots: see local files.

## How

- `CopyButton`: compact mode uses `size-3.5` icons; the labelled (non-compact) button keeps `size-3`.
- `TurnActions`: `Undo2` to `size-3.5`; `TurnDuration` rendered after the rollback tooltip, before the hover timestamp.
- User message `Pencil` to `size-3.5` to match its compact copy neighbour.
- Tests in `ChatTimelineItems.test.tsx` and `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` now assert the duration follows copy.
- The compact `CopyButton` is shared, so the copy icon in the script run panel is 14px too; its two snapshots are updated.

## Testing

1. Open the desktop app and open a chat session.
2. Send a short prompt that needs no tools (e.g. "say hi"). Under the reply, the row shows copy, roll back, then the duration.
3. Send a prompt that runs a tool. That reply shows "Worked for …" above, and copy / roll back sit at the same horizontal spot as in step 2.
4. Compare icon sizes: copy and roll back are visibly larger than before (14px). Hover a sent message: edit and copy icons are the same 14px size.
5. Click copy on a reply: the check mark shows at the same size, in green.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

fix: list assistant sessions under the agent the assistant acts as

Fixes [DNO-1500](https://linear.app/speakeasy/issue/DNO-1500/agent-identity-pages-show-no-sessions-for-assistant-backed-agents)

## Why

An agent identity that an assistant acts as showed "No sessions from this agent in this window", even when the assistant had sessions. The agent filter on `chats.list` matched only `chats.agent_id`, which only hook capture stamps. Assistant runtime chats never get that stamp: they reach their agent through the assistant's binding.

## What changed

The agent filter in `ListChats` and `CountChats` now also matches chats on a live thread of the assistant bound to the agent. The lookup starts from the binding's unique live-agent index, so it costs one indexed lookup per query. Hook-stamped sessions match as before. A new test covers both kinds of session and the `CountChats` page-past-the-end total.

**Before:** the agent's Overview, its Sessions tab and Agent Sessions filtered to the agent are all empty.

**After:** all three list the assistant's session.

The local demo seed already has an identity-bound assistant with a session, so the recordings below use it.

## Recordings

Before (Agent Sessions → agent identity Overview → Sessions → filtered Agent Sessions):

After (same path):

conf: fix two misspelled keys in the default aptly.conf

## Requirements

All new code should be covered with tests, documentation should be updated. CI should pass.

## Description of the Change

Since the YAML config became the default (9d0c7b5a), `debian/aptly.conf` has spelled two keys differently from the config struct:

| `debian/aptly.conf` | read by aptly |
| --- | --- |
| `dep_follow_allvariants` | `dep_follow_all_variants` |
| `dep_verbose_resolve` | `dep_verboseresolve` |

The YAML loader ignores unknown keys, so setting either to `true` in a config written from this template does nothing. On master, a config with the template spellings set to `true` shows both as `false` in `aptly config show -yaml`, and the struct spellings show `true`.

This renames both keys in `debian/aptly.conf` and in `CreateConfigTest_gold`, which mirrors it. Existing configs are unaffected; to make either setting take effect in one, rename the key. The `t02_config` system tests pass locally.

## Checklist

- [x] allow Maintainers to edit PR (rebase, run coverage, help with tests, ...)
- [ ] unit-test added (if change is algorithm)
- [x] functional test added/updated (if change is functional)
- [ ] man page updated (if applicable)
- [ ] bash completion updated (if applicable)
- [x] documentation updated
- [ ] author name in `AUTHORS`

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(storage): surface rows.Err() before caching signer info verdicts

## Problem

`GetExistingSignerInfo` caches a definitive `true`/`false` for every identity it is asked about. The FSC `rowIterator` never consults `rows.Err()`, so a scan cut short by a connection reset or statement timeout ends the reduce with a **nil error and a short result set**.

The cache loop then wrote `false` for identities whose signer info *is* stored. `SignerInfoExists` and `identity.Provider.AreMe` kept answering "not mine" for a genuine signer until the entry was evicted — blocking signing and ownership checks on an already-healthy database.

## Fix

Check `rows.Err()` after the reduce and before the cache loop: a truncated scan returns an error and leaves the cache untouched, so the next call re-queries.

## Tests

`identity_signerinfo_test.go` — truncated scan, complete scan, query error. The truncated-scan test fails without the fix (verified) and pins via `RowsWillBeClosed` that the rows are already released by `ReduceValue`'s deferred `Close`.

## Known limit (pre-existing, not addressed here)

This guarantees only that a *failed* read caches nothing. A **completed** read can still cache a stale verdict: the query and the cache write are separate steps, so a `StoreSignerInfo` committing between them is overwritten by the read's older `false`. Confirmed to reproduce identically before this change, so it is out of scope — filed as #2586.

Fixes #2562

+/*

+
+package common
+
+import (
+	"database/sql"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/DATA-DOG/go-sqlmock"
+	tdriver "github.com/LFDT-Panurus/panurus/token/driver"
+	cache2 "github.com/LFDT-Panurus/panurus/token/services/utils/cache"
+	"github.com/hyperledger-labs/fabric-smart-client/pkg/utils/errors"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+type recordingCache struct {
+	entries map[string]bool
+	adds    []string
+}
+
+func newRecordingCache() *recordingCache {
+	return &recordingCache{entries: map[string]bool{}}
+}
+
+func (c *recordingCache) Get(key string) (bool, bool) {
+	v, ok := c.entries[key]
+
+	return v, ok
+}
+
+func (c *recordingCache) GetOrLoad(key string, loader func() (bool, error)) (bool, bool, error) {
+	if v, ok := c.entries[key]; ok {
+		return v, true, nil
+	}
+	v, err := loader()
+	if err != nil {
+		return false, false, err
+	}
+	c.Add(key, v)
+
+	return v, false, nil
+}
+
+func (c *recordingCache) Add(key string, value bool) {
+	c.entries[key] = value
+	c.adds = append(c.adds, key)
+}
+
+func (c *recordingCache) Delete(key string) {
+	delete(c.entries, key)
+}
+
+const signersSelect = "SELECT identity_hash FROM SIGNERS WHERE \\(identity_hash\\) IN \\(\\(\\$1\\), \\(\\$2\\), \\(\\$3\\)\\)"
+
+func newSignerInfoStore(t *testing.T, signerInfoCache cache[bool]) *sqlFixture[*IdentityStore] {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	return newSQLFixture(t, func(db *sql.DB, _ sqlmock.Sqlmock) *IdentityStore {
+		return &IdentityStore{
+			readDB:          db,
+			writeDB:         db,
+			table:           identityTables{IdentityInfo: "ID_INFO", Signers: "SIGNERS"},
+			ci:              newTestInterpreter(),
+			signerInfoCache: signerInfoCache,
+			auditInfoCache:  cache2.NewNoCache[[]byte](),
+			errorWrapper:    passthroughErrorWrapper{},
+		}
+	})
+}
+
+func threeSigners() ([]tdriver.Identity, []string) {
+	ids := []tdriver.Identity{[]byte("alice"), []byte("bob"), []byte("carol")}
+	hashes := make([]string, len(ids))
+	for i, id := range ids {
+		hashes[i] = id.UniqueID()
+	}
+
+	return ids, hashes
+}
+
+// Regression test for #2562: the scan must fail, not the query.
+func TestGetExistingSignerInfo_TruncatedScanIsAnError(t *testing.T) {
+	signerInfoCache := newRecordingCache()
+	f := newSignerInfoStore(t, signerInfoCache)
+	ids, hashes := threeSigners()
+
+	f.mock.ExpectQuery(signersSelect).
+		WithArgs(hashes[0], hashes[1], hashes[2]).
+		WillReturnRows(sqlmock.NewRows([]string{"identity_hash"}).
+			AddRow(hashes[0]).
+			AddRow(hashes[1]).
+			AddRow(hashes[2]).
+			RowError(1, errors.New("connection reset by peer"))).
+		RowsWillBeClosed()
+
+	existing, err := f.store.GetExistingSignerInfo(t.Context(), ids...)
+
+	require.Error(t, err, "a scan truncated by a connection failure must be reported, not read as an empty tail")
+	require.ErrorContains(t, err, "connection reset by peer")
+	require.Nil(t, existing)
+	require.Empty(t, signerInfoCache.adds,
+		"nothing may be cached from a truncated scan: caching false for an unreached row makes a real signer permanently invisible")
+	require.NoError(t, f.mock.ExpectationsWereMet())
+}
+
+func TestGetExistingSignerInfo_CachesVerdictsOnCompleteScan(t *testing.T) {
+	signerInfoCache := newRecordingCache()
+	f := newSignerInfoStore(t, signerInfoCache)
+	ids, hashes := threeSigners()
+
+	f.mock.ExpectQuery(signersSelect).
+		WithArgs(hashes[0], hashes[1], hashes[2]).
+		WillReturnRows(sqlmock.NewRows([]string{"identity_hash"}).
+			AddRow(hashes[0]).
+			AddRow(hashes[2]))
+
+	existing, err := f.store.GetExistingSignerInfo(t.Context(), ids...)
+
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.ElementsMatch(t, []string{hashes[0], hashes[2]}, existing)
+	require.Equal(t, map[string]bool{hashes[0]: true, hashes[1]: false, hashes[2]: true}, signerInfoCache.entries)
+
+	// Served from the cache: ExpectationsWereMet fails if a second query is issued.
+	existing, err = f.store.GetExistingSignerInfo(t.Context(), ids...)
+
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.ElementsMatch(t, []string{hashes[0], hashes[2]}, existing)
+	require.NoError(t, f.mock.ExpectationsWereMet())
+}
+
+func TestGetExistingSignerInfo_QueryErrorIsReported(t *testing.T) {
+	signerInfoCache := newRecordingCache()
+	f := newSignerInfoStore(t, signerInfoCache)
+	ids, hashes := threeSigners()
+
+	f.mock.ExpectQuery(signersSelect).
+		WithArgs(hashes[0], hashes[1], hashes[2]).
+		WillReturnError(errors.New("statement timeout"))
+
+	existing, err := f.store.GetExistingSignerInfo(t.Context(), ids...)
+
+	require.ErrorContains(t, err, "statement timeout")
+	require.Nil(t, existing)
+	require.Empty(t, signerInfoCache.adds)
+	require.NoError(t, f.mock.ExpectationsWereMet())
+}

fix(ui): follow the clients alone on the screen of a client when the cluster refuses its allocations

## What changes

The screen of a client no longer warns and polls every 2 seconds with a token that may read jobs in some namespaces only. It follows Allocation and Node in every namespace, a stream such a token is refused since hashicorp/nomad#25089.

- When the cluster refuses that stream, with an error such as a 403 or by ending it within 5 seconds with no event (Nomad 2.0), the screen follows the clients alone, with no warning, the way the client list does since #169. Its allocations are then read on the 30 s poll and whenever a client changes.
- A refusal of the clients too warns and polls as before, and a stream that worked and then dropped is a drop, not a refusal.
- Each time the screen opens it asks for both again; the fallback of the client list does not carry over to it.
- docs/configuration.md says this.

Left as they are: the jobs of a node pool and screens with the session in all namespaces ask for every namespace too, and with such a token still warn and poll fast. They have no smaller set of topics to follow.

Closes #186

## Checklist

- [x] The test for this change was written first and failed
- [x] `make check` is green
- [x] The title is a conventional commit: `feat(ui): ...`, `fix(nomad): ...`

+				asked = append(asked, topics)
+				if slices.Contains(topics, nomad.TopicAllocation) {
+					return refuse()
+				}
+
+				return newChanges().stream(), nil
+			}
